rows: Baseball-size hail was reported by a NWS employee driving through the area. Report relayed by Midland NWS.
Breckenridge Police Department reported penny-size hail at Tanglewood Island on Hubbard Creek Reservoir.
Breckenridge PD reported several trees down in town.
Reported on the west side of Breckenridge.

Based on ground and aerial surveys...it was determined a tornado formed along FM 576 east of Eolian. The tornado damaged trees and a shed west of FM 576 and FM 3418 and continued to damage a large metal building on FM 3418. In addition, several large storage containers were blown…

The second tornado began approximately a half mile west of Highway 183 and south of FM 2231. Power poles were damaged along FM 2231 and Highway 183 and roof and barn damage was noted along Highway 183. The most significant damage occurred at and just west of the Stephens County A…
Storm chasers observed a brief tornado between Breckenridge and Caddo. The tornado was over open country and no damage was reported.
Golfball-size hail was reported on FM 2231.
Golfball size hail was reported in Necessity.
A spotter reported Grapefruit size hail on Highway 207 5 miles west of Strawn. The spotter received damage to their vehicle.
Golfball size hail covered the ground east of Caddo inside the Stephens county line.
Golfball size hail was reported in Caddo.
Baseball size hail was reported 5 miles south of Caddo.
Nickel size hail fell 4 miles south of Caddo.
Baseball size hail 4 miles south of Caddo.
Nickel size hail was reported in Gunsight.

Quarter size hail fell along County Road 215 one mile south of Highway 180.

Nickel size hail fell 3 miles west of Breckenridge on Highway 180.
Large tree limbs had to be removed off FM 1852 near Wayland.
Tree limbs were down in Caddo near State Park Road 33 and Highway 180.
The automated weather station at Stephens County Airport in Breckenridge (KBKD) measured a 58 mph wind gust.
Nickel size hail was reported eight miles southwest of the city of Breckenridge.
Numerous tree limbs were broken off in Breckenridge due to thunderstorm winds that were estimated at 60 mph.
Golfball sized hail fell at the intersection of Farm-to-Market 1853 and County Road 190.
Hen egg sized hail fell about 1 mile east-northeast of the town of Harpersville.
A brief tornado touched down approximately 2 miles east of Eliasville in extreme northern Stephens County.
The sheriff's office reported a vehicle was almost blown off the road by strong thunderstorms winds.
Several roofs of homes were damaged between Breckenridge and Crystal Falls. Trees were also blown down.
Quarter sized hail was reported at the Hubbard Creek Lake bridge west of Breckenridge.
Half-dollar sized hail was reported on the eastern side of Hubbard Creek Lake.

Several 3 inch diameter tree limbs, about 10 feet long, were blown down on the northwest side of Breckenridge.

A tree was uprooted 6 miles south of Breckenridge.
The KBKD AWOS recorded a 60 mph wind gust due to outflow winds ahead of a line of strong storms.
Penny sized hail was reported at Hubbard Creek Reservoir.
Law enforcement reported that a foreman construction trailer was destroyed at the new Walmart construction site.
Halfway between Breckenridge and Caddo, a garage door was damaged and an out building was moved.
A telephone pole was snapped in half and shingles were torn off the roof of a home. Also, a horse trailer was moved 30 feet, and the roof was ripped off of a wellhouse.

The Stephens County Sheriff's Department reported golf ball sized hail in Breckenridge, TX.
Emergency management reported that large trees were blown down on Park Road 33.
Golf ball sized hail was reported, approximately 10 miles southeast of Caddo.

A 60 mph wind gust was estimated in Breckenridge.

Law enforcement reports power lines down in Breckenridge.
One inch hail reported in Breckenridge.

Emergency management reported downed utility poles just southwest of the city of Ivan, TX.
Emergency management reported that a dead tree was blown onto a parked car in the city of Breckenridge, TX.
Emergency management reported 2 power lines down and 1 broken telephone pole in the northwest portion of the city of Breckenridge, TX.
Emergency management reported a large metal barn flipped on the northern side of the city of Breckenridge, TX.

Emergency management reported a roof blown off of a home just northwest of the city of Breckenridge, TX.
Nickel to quarter sized hail was reported 12 miles east of Breckenridge.

A severe thunderstorm developed in Shackelford County, then moved northeast into western Stephens County. The storm crossed Hubbard Creek Reservoir before gaining additional rotation evident on radar. As the storm moved into northern Stephens County, a tornado developed near Crys…
Quarter size hail was reported 10 miles south of Woodson.
Two inch hail was reported at the Stephens County Airport.
A picture of a hail stone that was slightly smaller than a baseball was sent in 4 miles southeast of Breckenridge.

Thunderstorm winds damaged trees around and to the west of the A&E Ranch entrance near CR 102 and Highway 180. In addition, a salt water storage tank was tipped over near the entrance of the ranch. Radar evidence suggests the tornadic development process may have been in progress…
Thunderstorm winds damaged trees for several miles along FM 207 to the southeast of Breckenridge. Tree damage was also observed to the east of the road into neighboring properties.
A trained spotter reported golf ball sized hail about a mile west of Breckenridge, TX.
Amateur radio reported baseball sized hail about 3 miles east of Breckenridge along Highway 180.
A social media video indicated large tree branches blown down at a rest area near the Stephens County line, or just southwest of Hubbard Creek Lake.
Notable damage was reported along FM 576 due to damaging straight line winds. A few roofs were removed from homes, metal doors were blown in, outbuilding and trees were damaged.
Damage to trees and outbuildings was reported in Necessity.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in Breckenridge.
The Breckenridge Airport AWOS measured 54 kts of wind.
Golf ball sized hail was reported outside of Caddo.
Public report of tennis-ball sized hail in southeast Stephens County, 10 miles north northwest of Ranger, TX.
A Facebook post reported 1 to 2 inch diameter hail in Gunsight.
A Facebook post reported golf ball sized hail around 5 miles south of Wayland.
A Facebook post reported 1.5 inch hail in south Necessity.
A member of the public reported 2 inch diameter hail on Hubbard Creek Lake.
Facebook report of large amounts of quarter size hail on CR 215.

Quarter sized hail was reported in Harpersville.

Social media images showed a small metal shed that was destroyed. Scattered large tree limbs were also down.
